findings.text: — §10's answer test reads back through `read_plan_review`, which selects the newest candidate by mtime (`plan_review.py:1036`, `_candidate_paths` enumerates staging beside the committed tree at `plan_review.py:617-654`); a `record_response` that writes staging only leaves the staging file newer than the committed copy, so `read_plan_review` returns the staging record carrying the answer and `unanswered_findings` is empty — reproduced: with the committed record written first and a staging copy answered second (mtime 1791372032820189059 > 1791372032769186267), `read_plan_review("probe","demo",3)` returned `responses={'f1': {...}}` and `unanswered_findings([])`. The declared control "it fails when `record_response` writes staging only" therefore cannot turn the test red; the shadowing is real but only for the committed-first readers (`stored_record`, `list_plan_reviews`/`review_coverage`, which is what the dispatch gate reads), not for the reader the done-when names. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — the node would be briefed to prove its guard with a reader that cannot exhibit the defect, so the test would pass against the unfixed code or be silently redirected; the done-when must name a committed-first reader (the gate's `review_coverage` path) or the plan must state which reader is shadowed.

— §10's Why grounds the whole section on "readers read a review's committed record before its staging copy, and two writers change a record after it was stored", but that premise is false for `read_plan_review`, the reader §10's done-when then relies on: `read_plan_review` returns the newest record by mtime, not the committed copy. The plan's root cause is right for the committed-first gate reader but its stated premise is stated unconditionally and is contradicted by its own named reader and cited code. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — naming which reader is shadowed (the committed-first gate reader) is what makes the done-when's test sound; leaving the premise unconditional is what produced the unmakable control above.

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §10's answer test names `read_plan_review` as the reader that shows the shadowing, but `read_plan_review` returns the newest candidate by mtime (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:1036`), so the staging-only answer it writes is the newest file and reads back fine; the declared control "it fails when `record_response` writes staging only" cannot fire.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §10 names no session scratchpad or node-local temporary path; its tests are run by the node it dispatches.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §10 carries no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags into code, and its prose states the mechanism rather than a changelog.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §10's Why asserts as a premise that "readers read a review's committed record before its staging copy", but that holds only for the committed-first readers (`stored_record`, `list_plan_reviews`, `review_coverage`); `read_plan_review`, the reader the done-when relies on, orders by file mtime and returns the staging copy. The section's own premise and its named reader disagree.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §10 names one node and states one goal, that a disposition or answer written around promotion is not shadowed; the three done-when tests are three faces of that one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §10 declares no depends-on, and its shared write of `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` with §8 node (1) and §9 (a)/(d) is serialized by the dispatch scope check, so no plan-level edge is required (the same ground on which the earlier §9 wiring finding was declined); its real dependency, §3, is landed.
